title: Correlation-sensitive magic-state distillation from spin-squeezed neutral atoms
authors: Ximo Wang, Ruyue Guo, Xinbo Li, Min Feng, Haozhe Wang, Zhenqi Bai, Yichi Zhang
abstract: We show that interblock correlations can reverse magic-state distillation even when every input exceeds the threshold for independent states. For the five-to-one Bravyi-Kitaev protocol with independent local Clifford twirls, we express the output in terms of measurable target-axis moments. Fourth-order correlations determine acceptance, while third- and fifth-order correlations determine the output polarization. This relation yields a direct sign test for distillation gain and opposite gains for inputs with identical single-qubit and two-qubit reduced states. We connect this mechanism to neutral-atom resource preparation through finite-range Ising dynamics. Block separation suppresses detrimental interblock coupling, and locally addressed Clifford phases release interaction-generated magic from a spin-squeezed precursor by changing the symmetry selected by code projection. A protocol that retains accepted source outputs achieves positive gain above a source-contrast threshold set by circuit errors and storage dephasing. The same moments specify a finite-sample experimental diagnostic. These results connect the correlation structure of a resource state to its preparation, acceptance, and distillation gain.
summary: This paper introduces a correlation-sensitive diagnostic for magic-state distillation in spin-squeezed neutral atoms. It shows that higher-order correlations, not just single- or two-qubit measurements, are necessary to accurately predict the distillation gain. This provides a crucial theoretical link between the correlation structure of the physical resource state and its ultimate utility in quantum computation.
main_problem: The research addresses developing a correlation-sensitive method for magic-state distillation, aiming to predict distillation gain even when input states exceed the threshold for independent states.
main_result: Interblock correlations can reverse magic-state distillation, and higher-order moments provide a necessary diagnostic to predict distillation gain, which is otherwise obscured by identical low-order reduced states.
method: The authors derive the correlated-input Bravyi–Kitaev map and use higher-order Pauli string expectation values (third- and fifth-order correlations) to determine the sign of the distillation gain.
model_or_system: The process is modeled using five-to-one magic-state distillation protocols applied to spin-squeezed neutral atoms, utilizing finite-range Ising dynamics for resource preparation.
key_observables: Distillation Gain ($G$), Acceptance Probability ($	ext{pacc}$), Output Polarization (determined by third- and fifth-order correlations), and various higher-order Pauli string moments ($A_k$).
important_parameters: Block separation ($s$), circuit error rates, storage dephasing rates, and the source-contrast threshold.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes a circuit model incorporating readout errors, loss, and storage histories, and that the gain is determined by higher-order correlations.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the five-to-one distillation process, the encoding hierarchy, and the dependence of distillation gain ($G$) on higher-order moments and the physical separation ($s$) between atomic blocks.
paper_structure: The paper builds from the theoretical framework of correlated distillation protocols, details the physical implementation using spin-squeezed atoms and Ising dynamics, derives the necessary moment-based diagnostics, and concludes by linking these statistical measures to physical parameters like block separation and error rates.
why_interesting: This work directly bridges the gap between the fundamental quantum resource theory (magic-state distillation) and the physical implementation constraints of neutral atom arrays, providing a quantitative diagnostic tool based on higher-order correlations.
